title: GEOMLAMA: Geo-Diverse Commonsense Probing on Multilingual Pre-Trained Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Probing multilingual PLMs with masked templates querying region-specific commonsense knowledge across five countries (US, China, India, Iran, Kenya), both with explicit country cues and with the cues removed to measure intrinsic regional inclinations.

Evaluating model predictions on culture-specific practices, habits, and customs (e.g., traditional wedding dress colors, staple foods) to see if models default to Western-centric norms or recognize diverse cultural concepts.

Comparing the accuracy of commonsense knowledge extraction when querying the models using prompts translated into five different languages (English, Chinese, Hindi, Persian, Swahili) to determine if performance relies heavily on the probing language.

Analyzing word co-occurrence frequencies in language-specific corpora (e.g., English vs. Chinese Wikipedia) to demonstrate that obvious local commonsense is often under-reported in a country's native language.
